notes: Dev RBox contraction, paired with the revision literature_arts-replace-d006 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): it removes the property that revision changes, 'Corresponded with' is symmetric (staging/literature_arts.RELATIONS.md). It replaces the earlier removal of Func(composed_by) (the pairing rule was added to the README on 2026-11-11); that version's review issues (a property that does not hold in general, real instances with stored attributions, a double negative, 能否 in Chinese) are avoided here. The instances are the revision's own, with made-up writers and artists given in the prompt (Wikipedia searches for the four names: 0 hits on 2026-11-11), so no stored fact about them competes with the property. They ask what is true of the converse ('Did Oskar Brandvik correspond with Marta Velling?') rather than 'does it follow that ...', which avoids the reading where, once the property is gone, the honest answer to 'does it follow' is 'no, it does not follow' rather than 'I don't know'. Both original answers are 'yes': a negated instance would be 'no' both before and after a removal, so it cannot balance a contraction. Every query becomes 'does not know': the direct question, the propositional ones (strong Kleene) and both instances. Residual risk, recorded: corresponding is exchanging letters, so a model may keep 'yes' from the word's meaning rather than the property; that is the property kept by another route, never a sign the removal worked. Near unrelated asks the same property of a neighbouring symmetric literature relation (co-wrote a book with: yes), the relation the paired revision's near query uses; collaborated_with was dropped there because the main split edits its property (literature 0010), and is dropped here for the same reason. Contraction is exempt from Rule 7. hops counts the prompt's premise as the bridge, as the template does. Tag for analysis (review 2026-11-12): this is a DEFINITIONAL removal. 'Exchanged letters with' makes the converse true by the meaning of the words, and 'corresponded with' in Chinese and Spanish ('通信', 'mantuvo correspondencia con') is two-way in the same way, so a 'yes' on the instances and cross-lingual questions can survive a clean removal. Slice these results as definitional and read them with that in mind. The prompts were not reworded to a one-directional 'wrote letters to': that is a different relation from the one whose property is removed, and the cross-lingual prompts must stay translations of the English question. The paired revision's relation is final, so the choice of a relation whose symmetry is contingent is left to the user. Review 2026-11-12: the direct question was reworded from "Is the relation 'corresponded with' symmetric?" (all four models answered no to the term) to the plain-language meaning of symmetry. Round 3 (2026-11-13): the direct question was reworded to a concrete case with the plain gloss 'they exchanged letters', after Qwen3, Olmo and Llama answered no or 'not necessarily' to the abstract form; the paired revision d006 uses the same frame.
